method: score-description.py --type self-contained --runs 3 --model opus --bar 7. Each of the 20 queries ran 3 times as a real nested `claude -p` with only this skill available; a run counts as TRIGGERED iff the model reaches for the skill among its first tool decisions. 60 subprocess calls total. Runs was set to 3 rather than the script's default 5 by explicit decision — the spend was approved on that basis.

results.note: The one miss, and it is not random. The description covers where a document belongs and how documentation is structured; it does not mention installing or wiring anything. An adoption-phrased request therefore finds nothing to match. The skill does carry an Install section in its body, so the capability exists and only the description omits it.

note_on_the_miss: Measured twice, and the miss moves — so it is run-to-run variance, not a hole in the description. First measurement missed an adoption-phrased request; a second measurement of the same queryset had that one firing and a different query missing instead, at 1/3. The same unchanged description scored 9.5 in one run and 10.0 in another. At three runs per query the fire/no-fire boundary is noisy enough that 11/12 and 12/12 are not distinguishable, so chasing the named miss would be fitting to noise.
note_on_automated_loop: No automated rewrite loop was run. The bar is 7.0 and the measured score is 9.5, so there was nothing to optimise toward — a rewrite loop here would risk regressing the 8/8 negative-hold in exchange for one phrasing.
note_on_a_reverted_attempt: One rewrite was tried and reverted. The description already named installation; the attempt made that clause more specific, matching the missed phrasing's own words. Result: the adoption query started firing, an unrelated query stopped, and the score came out 0.5 lower than the unchanged description in the same run — a regression by the tool's own gate. Reverted rather than kept, and recorded rather than quietly dropped. The negatives held 8/8 throughout, in every run.
variance_note: runs=3 per query. Distinguishing 11/12 from 12/12 would need 5 or more.
